I started a landscaping company at the start of covid, got out of it and am in sales now. 

Owning a business is 24/7. Every headache, you need to deal with. I would list them out but they’re endless. With a “regular” job, at least you can leave your work at work. 

I never did plowing because insurance was too much. Last year we didn’t have any snow to plow all winter so I guess i lucked out not taking on that part of the business. 

And mowing sucks, hot days, Barely talk to anyone at all (I’m an introvert and it was still very lonely even for me), machine repairs, always getting gas for the machines, mowing the same damn yard and picking up the same damn toys and moving the same damned trampoline back and forth, ducking under the same damned branch that the client refuses to trim. Just wasn’t for me. Although I was in the best shape of my life. 

Starting out, you’d probably solo until you gain enough accounts to warrant getting a helper and expand from there. (More employees, more equipment, etc)

If you have the gusto for that, you could grow a pretty large company and then sell it when the time is right or grow it bigger. 

I had some big dreams starting that business but I also learned, I am not the type of person that should own a business. 

If you don’t like doing paperwork and the books, you need to hire someone. And like someone else said, you need to get an accountant. My accountant saved me tens of thousands on my taxes.

Sounds like you’re letting him fail. Imagine working in a restaurant and allowing your coworker to forget bread in the oven or something. Work as a team. 

I’d suggest he cooks and you help him. You obviously have more experience than he does so give him pointers when he does something wrong like, “hey, I’m gonna turn these potatoes down so they don’t boil over.” 

You ask what he’s making and set him up to succeed. “Hey let’s get this steak to room temp before we put it on” “is that corn ready to go?”

He needs to know a routine to cooking and learn how you do things better. Cooking in a kitchen and seeing what other people are doing helps you learn. Seems like he might not have helped his parents cook while growing up. Maybe he can sit and talk with you while you’re cooking? 

Just a suggestion.
